regulations.name: ESPR – Digital Product Passport (framework)
regulations.description: The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation sets up the passport: a unique identifier, a data carrier (e.g. QR), registration in the EU DPP Registry and access rights. What goes in a passport, and from when, is set per product group by delegated acts. None of those acts has been adopted yet, so on its own this rule requires no passport: use these basics for a voluntary passport or to prepare early.
regulations.statusNote: In force since 18 Jul 2024 · passport content and dates set per product group

regulations.name: Textile Labelling – Fibre composition
regulations.description: Every textile product sold in the EU carries a label or marking with its full fibre composition: each fibre by its EU name (Annex I) and percentage by weight, in descending order. Products with non-textile parts of animal origin (leather trims, fur, bone buttons) must say so. Care symbols and country of origin are not required by EU law. A revision is expected alongside the ESPR textiles act.

requirements.name: Fibre composition
requirements.help: Every fibre by its EU name and % by weight, in descending order. Fibres of up to 5% each (15% together) that are hard to state may be grouped as “other fibres”. Enter them as the composition.

requirements.name: Durable fibre label
requirements.help: Art. 14 and 16: the label is durable, legible and securely attached, and the composition is in the official language(s) of each EU country where the product is sold.

requirements.name: Non-textile parts of animal origin
requirements.help: Art. 12: products with leather, fur, bone or horn parts say “Contains non-textile parts of animal origin” on the label.

requirements.name: Care instructions
requirements.help: Not required by EU law; most brands use the GINETEX / ISO 3758 care symbols.

regulations.name: France AGEC – Textile product information
regulations.reference: French Environment Code Art. L541-9-1 · Décret n° 2022-748
regulations.description: France’s anti-waste law (AGEC): companies selling new clothing, household linen and home textiles in France publish environmental information for each product on a product sheet online, free and easy to find. Phased in by size, counting sales in France: from 1 Jan 2023 above €50M turnover and 25,000 units a year; from 1 Jan 2024 above €20M and 10,000 units; from 1 Jan 2025 above €10M and 10,000 units. Smaller companies are not covered.
regulations.statusNote: Applies since 1 Jan 2023 · companies above €10M turnover and 10,000 units in France since 1 Jan 2025

regulations.name: RoHS – Hazardous substances in electronics
regulations.description: Limits lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE and four phthalates in electrical and electronic equipment.

requirements.name: Declaration of conformity covering RoHS
requirements.help: Usually part of your CE declaration. Keep the technical documentation (test reports) on file for the authorities.

regulations.name: REACH – Substances of very high concern
regulations.description: Articles containing a substance of very high concern (Candidate List) above 0.1% by weight must come with information on safe use; under the Waste Framework Directive, suppliers also notify such articles to ECHA’s SCIP database.

requirements.name: SVHC declaration
requirements.help: Declare Candidate List substances above 0.1%, or record that there are none.

requirements.name: SCIP notification
requirements.help: Waste Framework Directive, not REACH: needed only if an SVHC is present above 0.1%.

regulations.name: PPWR – Packaging declaration of conformity
regulations.description: Since 12 August 2026 all packaging placed on the EU market must meet the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. The brand whose name or trademark is on the packaging is its manufacturer (Art. 3(1)(13)): it assesses each packaging type itself (Annex VII), keeps the technical documentation and signs an EU declaration of conformity per packaging type (Art. 39, Annex VIII). Applies today: heavy metals at most 100 mg/kg (Art. 5(4)), PFAS limits for food-contact packaging (Art. 5(5)), recyclable design (Art. 6(1)) and re-use rules for reusable packaging (Art. 11). Micro-enterprises whose packaging supplier is in the same EU country can leave this to that supplier.
regulations.statusNote: Applies since 12 Aug 2026 · one declaration per packaging type

requirements.name: Packaging with a signed declaration of conformity
requirements.help: Each packaging type the product is sold in needs a current EU declaration of conformity, signed after its last change.
